title: Rebuilding the Old Town from 18th-century paintings
description: German forces levelled Warsaw’s Old Town after the 1944 Uprising. 99% Invisible, Roman Mars’s design show, tells how it was rebuilt from the 1940s using 18th-century views of the city by the painter Bernardo Bellotto, known as Canaletto.

title: A girl from Freta Street becomes the first woman to win a Nobel
description: Maria Skłodowska was born in 1867 on Freta Street in the New Town, studied at Warsaw’s illegal ‘Flying University’ and left for Paris, where she discovered polonium and radium. Her birthplace is now a small museum to her life.

title: A city besieged for three weeks in September 1939
episode: Hitler's War on Poland: The Fall of Warsaw (Part 3)
description: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on the German siege of Warsaw in 1939, when shelling and bombing set the Royal Castle on Castle Square ablaze, and the city’s surrender on 28 September after nearly three weeks of resistance.
spotify: The Rest is History Hitler's War on Poland: The Fall of Warsaw (Part 3)
apple: The Rest is History Hitler's War on Poland: The Fall of Warsaw (Part 3)

title: Sixty-three days of fighting for a city the Red Army watched
description: On 1 August 1944 the Home Army, Poland’s underground resistance, rose against the German occupiers and held out for 63 days while Soviet forces halted across the Vistula. The Warsaw Rising Museum, in an old tram power station in Wola, tells the story.
spotify: Dan Snow's History Hit The Warsaw Uprising
apple: Dan Snow's History Hit The Warsaw Uprising

title: Civilians killed street by street in the Uprising’s first week
description: In early August 1944, days into the Warsaw Uprising, German and collaborating units shot tens of thousands of civilians in the western district of Wola. History Hit’s Warfare show covers the massacre; a memorial now stands on Leszno Street.

title: Moscow signs up its satellites in a Warsaw palace
episode: The founding of the Warsaw Pact
description: On 14 May 1955 the Soviet Union and seven Eastern Bloc states signed a military alliance in Warsaw, a reply to West Germany joining NATO. The BBC’s Witness History hears the story; the treaty was signed in what is now the Presidential Palace.
